facts.meaning: command122 computes operand once before iterating the inclusive target variable range. Other selector7/subselector4 reads $stats.play_time; subselector3 reads computed distance_moved=sum walked+cycled+surfed, discovered outside original714. play_time getter can mutate stored play_time and temp uptime anchor before any variable write, or return cached value when no anchor. Per target operations set/add/subtract/multiply/divide/remainder skip their explicit no-op/bound/zero-or-one conditions, then clamp to +/-99999999 and request map refresh. No integer conversion is applied to play-time operand.

facts.failure_prefix: Getter can commit clock/anchor before invalid target operation. Earlier variables/refresh commit before a later variable raises. No rollback. Division type/result follows actual operand/runtime semantics, not a newly inferred integer guarantee.
facts.open: Game_Variables index/value filtering and native numeric coercion are their own contracts. Whole command dispatch/conditions/scripts and host clock execution remain outside this finite receipt.

facts.meaning: command124 start(parameter0==0) reads play_time and assigns GameSystem.timer_start, then timer_duration=parameter1; stop assigns start=nil and does not change duration. timer getter returns0 without start or stats, otherwise duration-currentplaytime+start, with no zero clamp. Thus repeated timer reads may advance Stats through its getter and elapsed timer may become negative.
facts.control: A numeric start0 is truthy under this source language; stop nil is the explicit inactive representation. Actual duration validity is not guarded here.
facts.failure_prefix: Stats getter update precedes timer_start assignment; start assignment precedes duration assignment. Later failure can leave the new start with old duration. Stop does not query play_time. No ensure/rollback.
facts.open: Timer display/countdown-event behavior, native timing and loaded object invariants require independent consumers; no wall-clock accuracy or all GameSystem acceptance.

facts.meaning: pbPushThisEvent captures coordinates then strict passability-checks player direction; failure returns before counter. Success increments strength_push_count before dispatching one of four move methods, even when strength argumentfalse. It requests map moved-event tracking regardless of observed coordinate change. Only changed coordinates optionally play Strength SE, lock player, loop Graphics/Input/map updates until movement stops, then unlock. pbPushThisBoulder invokes only when strengthUsed but returns true regardless.
facts.control: Counter measures accepted push attempts at this location, not proven moved distance, completed animation or only Strength-labeled calls. Nonstandard direction with a truthy passability result can increment without matching move arm. No counter is incremented when strict passability returns false.
facts.failure_prefix: Counter increments before movement/native sound/lock/loop, so subsequent failure retains it. Loop failure after lock can leave player locked; unlock has no ensure. Tracking can fail after move but before visual loop.
facts.open: Strict passability implementation/map movement/animation completion and all movement event callbacks remain independently scoped. No execution or new formal finding is inferred from counter name.
